2585: /// The token reserved in the lock when the write permission is given out.

2588: /// Half of the permission for read access, one for `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` and the other for all `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2589: type HalfPerm<T> = Count<PointsTo<T>>;

2591: /// The permission for read access can be further split into `MAX_READER` pieces.
2592: type ReadPerm<T> = (HalfPerm<T>, OneLeftKnowledge<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>);

2594: tracked struct RwPerms<T> {
2595:     /// This token tracks whether the write permission is given out. If it is `Left`, it stores the knowledge that
2596:     /// there are active readers because the existence of `HalfPerm` resource for read access.
2597:     /// If it is `Right`, we know there is an active writer and there is no active reader, because there is a `NoPerm`
2598:     /// indicating the absence of `PointsTo<T>`.
2599:     core_token: SumResource<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>,
2600:     /// The permission to retract a `READER` count. Its total quantity tracks the gap between
2601:     /// the number of `try_read` increments recorded in the lock atomic and the number of active
2602:     /// `RwLockReadGuard`s (created and ongoing creation that will succeed) represented by `read_guard_token`.
2603:     /// It can be splited up to `V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS:= 2 * MAX_READER` pieces,
2604:     /// which allows at most `2*MAX_READER - 1` `try_read` attempts that will fail to acquire the lock.
2605:     read_retract_token: TokenResource<V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS>,
2606:     /// The permission to retract the set of `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit.
2607:     upread_retract_token: Option<UniqueToken>,
2608:     /// Tracks whether there is a live `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, also stores half of the permission for read access.
2609:     upreader_guard_token: Option<OneLeftOwner<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>>,
2610:     /// Tracks the number of live `RwLockReadGuard`s. If it is `Left`, it stores the remaining read permissions.
2611:     /// If it is `Right`, it stores an empty token indicating the permission has been given out.
2612:     read_guard_token: Sum<
2613:         CountResource<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,
2614:         EmptyCount<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,

2701: struct_with_invariants! {
2702: /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2703: ///
2704: /// # Overview
2705: ///
2706: /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2707: /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2708: /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2709: /// read-only access.
2710: ///
2711: /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2712: /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2713: /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2714: /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2715: /// the cost of spinning.
2716: ///
2717: /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2718: /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2719: /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2720: /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2721: ///
2722: /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2723: /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2724: /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2725: /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2726: /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2727: /// while the lock is held.
2728: ///
2729: /// # Usage
2730: /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2731: /// but written to occasionally.
2732: ///
2733: /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2734: /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2735: ///
2736: /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2737: /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2738: ///
2739: /// # About Guard
2740: ///
2741: /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2742: ///
2743: /// # Examples
2744: ///
2745: /// ```
2746: /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2747: ///
2748: /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2749: ///
2750: /// // many read locks can be held at once
2751: /// {
2752: ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2753: ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2754: ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2755: ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2756: ///
2757: ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2758: ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2759: ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2760: ///     drop(r1);
2761: ///     drop(r2);
2762: ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2763: ///
2764: ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2765: ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2766: ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2767: ///     *w1 += 1;
2768: ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
2769: /// }   // upread lock are dropped at this point
2770: ///
2771: /// {
2772: ///     // Only one write lock can be held at a time
2773: ///     let mut w2 = lock.write();
2774: ///     *w2 += 1;
2775: ///     assert_eq!(*w2, 7);
2776: /// }   // write lock is dropped at this point
2777: /// ```
2778: ///
2779: /// [`SpinLock`]: super::SpinLock
2780: pub struct RwLock<T  /* : ?Sized*/ , Guard /* = PreemptDisabled*/ > {
2781:     guard: PhantomData<Guard>,
2782:     /// The internal representation of the lock state is as follows:
2783:     /// - **Bit 63:** Writer lock.
2784:     /// - **Bit 62:** Upgradeable reader lock.
2785:     /// - **Bit 61:** Indicates if an upgradeable reader is being upgraded.
2786:     /// - **Bits 60-0:** Reader lock count.
2787:     lock: AtomicUsize<_, RwPerms<T>,_>,
2788:     // val: UnsafeCell<T>,
2789:     val: PCell<T>,
2790:     ghost_id: Ghost<RwId>,
2791: }
2792: 
2793: /// This invariant holds at any time, i.e. not violated during any method execution.
2794: closed spec fn wf(self) -> bool {
2795:     invariant on lock with (val, guard, ghost_id) is (v: usize, g: RwPerms<T>) {
2796:         // BITS VALUE
2797:         let has_writer_bit: bool = (v & WRITER) != 0;
2798:         let has_upgrade_bit: bool = (v & UPGRADEABLE_READER) != 0;
2799:         let has_max_reader_bit: bool = (v & MAX_READER) != 0;
2800:         // The total number of `try_read` attempts recorded in the lock atomic, including created `RwLockReadGuard`s
2801:         // and those who are trying, no matter they will succeed or fail.
2802:         let total_reader_bits: int = (v & MAX_READER_MASK) as int;
2803:         // The clamped value represented in the counter bits. This counts the maximum number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2804:         // NOTE: This does not mean there are actually this number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s. The actual number of successfully
2805:         // created/creating `RwLockReadGuard`s can be smaller than this number, because previously created `RwLockReadGuard`s may be dropped.
2806:         let reader_bits: int = if has_max_reader_bit { MAX_READER as int } else { (v & READER_MASK) as int };
2807: 
2808:         // ACTUAL NUMBER OF ACTIVE GUARDS.
2809:         // The number is tracked by the ghost resources remained in the lock.
2810:         // By active, we mean from the perspective the lock, the permissions for these guards are given out.
2811:         // The actual guards may be still being created, but they must be successfully created finally.
2812:         // This invariant maintains the consistency between the ghost resources and the lock atomic value.
2813: 
2814:         // Whether there is an active writer
2815:         let active_writer: bool = g.core_token.is_right();
2816:         // The number of active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, which can only be 0 or 1.
2817:         let active_upgrade_guard: bool = !active_writer && g.upreader_guard_token is None;
2818:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2819:         let active_read_guards: int = if g.read_guard_token is Left {
2820:             MAX_READER_U64 - g.read_guard_token.left().frac()
2821:         } else {
2822:             0
2823:         };
2824:         // The first `try_upread` that fails, which has not returned yet.
2825:         let pending_failed_upread_attempt: bool = g.upread_retract_token is None;
2826:         // The number of `try_read` attempts that will fail.
2827:         let failed_reader_attempts: int = V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS - g.read_retract_token.frac();
2828: 
2829:         &&& if g.core_token.is_left() {
2830:             g.read_guard_token is Left
2831:         } else {
2832:             &&& g.upreader_guard_token is None
2833:             &&& g.read_guard_token is Right
2834:         }
2835:         // The `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit is set iff there is an active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` or a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2836:         &&& has_upgrade_bit <==> (active_upgrade_guard || pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2837:         // An active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` cannot coexist with a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2838:         &&& !(active_upgrade_guard && pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2839:         // The `READER` bits count the number of all active read guards and pending failed `try_read` attempts.
2840:         &&& total_reader_bits == active_read_guards + failed_reader_attempts
2841:         // There is an active `RwLockWriteGuard` iff the `WRITER` bit is set.
2842:         &&& active_writer <==> has_writer_bit
2843:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGaurd`s is less than or equal to the `READER` bits.
2844:         &&& 0 <= active_read_guards <= reader_bits <= total_reader_bits
2845:         // The core invariant of `RwLock`: there are no simultaneous active writers and readers.
2846:         &&& !(active_writer && (active_read_guards + if active_upgrade_guard { 1int } else { 0 }) > 0)
2847:         &&& g.core_token.id() == ghost_id@.core_token_id
2848:         &&& g.core_token.wf()
2849:         &&& g.core_token.is_left() ==> {
2850:             &&& !g.core_token.is_resource_owner()
2851:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 1
2852:         }
2853:         &&& g.core_token.is_right() ==> {
2854:             let empty = g.core_token.resource_right();
2855:             &&& empty.id() == ghost_id@.frac_id
2856:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 2
2857:             &&& g.core_token.has_resource()
2858:         }
2859:         &&& g.read_retract_token.wf()
2860:         &&& g.read_retract_token.id() == ghost_id@.read_retract_token_id
2861:         &&& g.upread_retract_token is Some ==>
2862:             {
2863:                 let token = g.upread_retract_token->0;
2864:                 &&& token.wf()
2865:                 &&& token.id() == ghost_id@.upread_retract_token_id
2866:             }
2867:         &&& g.upreader_guard_token is Some ==> {
2868:             let token = g.upreader_guard_token->0;
2869:             wf_upgradeable_guard_token(ghost_id@.core_token_id, ghost_id@.frac_id, val.id(), token)
2870:         }
2871:         &&& match g.read_guard_token {
2872:             Sum::Left(token) => {
2873:                 &&& token.wf()
2874:                 &&& token.id() == ghost_id@.read_guard_token_id
2875:                 &&& token.not_empty() ==> {
2876:                     let resource = token.resource();
2877:                     let read_half_cell_perm = resource.0;
2878:                     let mode_knowledge = resource.1;
2879:                     &&& mode_knowledge.id() == ghost_id@.core_token_id
2880:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.id() == ghost_id@.frac_id
2881:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.resource().id() == val.id()
2882:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.frac() == 1
2883:                 }
2884:             },
2885:             Sum::Right(empty) => {
2886:                 &&& empty.id() == ghost_id@.read_guard_token_id
2887:             },
2888:         }
2889: 
2890:     }
2891: }
2892: 
2893: }

2987:     /// Acquires a read lock and spin-wait until it can be acquired.
2988:     ///
2989:     /// The calling thread will spin-wait until there are no writers or
2990:     /// upgrading upreaders present. There is no guarantee for the order
2991:     /// in which other readers or writers waiting simultaneously will
2992:     /// obtain the lock.
2993:     #[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]
2994:     pub fn read(&self) -> RwLockReadGuard<'_, T, G> {
2995:         loop {
2996:             if let Some(readguard) = self.try_read() {
2997:                 return readguard;
2998:             } else {
2999:                 core::hint::spin_loop();
3000:             }
3001:         }
3002:     }

3004:     /// Acquires a write lock and spin-wait until it can be acquired.
3005:     ///
3006:     /// The calling thread will spin-wait until there are no other writers,
3007:     /// upreaders or readers present. There is no guarantee for the order
3008:     /// in which other readers or writers waiting simultaneously will
3009:     /// obtain the lock.
3010:     #[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]
3011:     pub fn write(&self) -> RwLockWriteGuard<'_, T, G> {
3012:         loop {
3013:             if let Some(writeguard) = self.try_write() {

2585: /// The token reserved in the lock when the write permission is given out.
2586: type NoPerm<T> = EmptyCount<PointsTo<T>>;
2587: /// Half of the permission for read access, one for `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` and the other for all `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2588: type HalfPerm<T> = Count<PointsTo<T>>;
2589: /// The permission for read access can be further split into `MAX_READER` pieces.
2590: type ReadPerm<T> = (HalfPerm<T>, OneLeftKnowledge<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>);
2591: 
2592: tracked struct RwPerms<T> {
2593:     /// This token tracks whether the write permission is given out. If it is `Left`, it stores the knowledge that
2594:     /// there are active readers because the existence of `HalfPerm` resource for read access.
2595:     /// If it is `Right`, we know there is an active writer and there is no active reader, because there is a `NoPerm`
2596:     /// indicating the absence of `PointsTo<T>`.
2597:     core_token: SumResource<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>,
2598:     /// The permission to retract a `READER` count. Its total quantity tracks the gap between
2599:     /// the number of `try_read` increments recorded in the lock atomic and the number of active
2600:     /// `RwLockReadGuard`s (created and ongoing creation that will succeed) represented by `read_guard_token`.
2601:     /// It can be splited up to `V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS:= 2 * MAX_READER` pieces,
2602:     /// which allows at most `2*MAX_READER - 1` `try_read` attempts that will fail to acquire the lock.
2603:     read_retract_token: TokenResource<V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS>,
2604:     /// The permission to retract the set of `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit.
2605:     upread_retract_token: Option<UniqueToken>,
2606:     /// Tracks whether there is a live `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, also stores half of the permission for read access.
2607:     upreader_guard_token: Option<OneLeftOwner<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>>,
2608:     /// Tracks the number of live `RwLockReadGuard`s. If it is `Left`, it stores the remaining read permissions.
2609:     /// If it is `Right`, it stores an empty token indicating the permission has been given out.
2610:     read_guard_token: Sum<
2611:         CountResource<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,
2612:         EmptyCount<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,
2613:     >,
2614: }

2624: /// The number of `try_read` operations recorded in the lock atomic (created and ongoing) can never reach `2*MAX_READER` to avoid overflow.
2625: /// **NOTE**: We *ASSUME* this property always holds without any proof. We believe this is true in practice because:
2626: /// - More than `2^61` `try_read` operations are required to trigger the overflow concurrently, which is absurd in real world scenarios.
2627: /// - If one tries to create a huge number (more than `2*MAX_READER`) of `RwLockReadGuard`s in a loop with `mem::forget`, it will take years and

2630:     v & MAX_READER_MASK < MAX_READER_MASK

2699: struct_with_invariants! {
2700: /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2701: ///
2702: /// # Overview
2703: ///
2704: /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2705: /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2706: /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2707: /// read-only access.
2708: ///
2709: /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2710: /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2711: /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2712: /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2713: /// the cost of spinning.
2714: ///
2715: /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2716: /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2717: /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2718: /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2719: ///
2720: /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2721: /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2722: /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2723: /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2724: /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2725: /// while the lock is held.
2726: ///
2727: /// # Usage
2728: /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2729: /// but written to occasionally.
2730: ///
2731: /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2732: /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2733: ///
2734: /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2735: /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2736: ///
2737: /// # About Guard
2738: ///
2739: /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2740: ///
2741: /// # Examples
2742: ///
2743: /// ```
2744: /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2745: ///
2746: /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2747: ///
2748: /// // many read locks can be held at once
2749: /// {
2750: ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2751: ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2752: ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2753: ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2754: ///
2755: ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2756: ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2757: ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2758: ///     drop(r1);
2759: ///     drop(r2);
2760: ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2761: ///
2762: ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2763: ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2764: ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2765: ///     *w1 += 1;
2766: ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
2767: /// }   // upread lock are dropped at this point
2768: ///
2769: /// {
2770: ///     // Only one write lock can be held at a time
2771: ///     let mut w2 = lock.write();
2772: ///     *w2 += 1;
2773: ///     assert_eq!(*w2, 7);
2774: /// }   // write lock is dropped at this point
2775: /// ```
2776: ///
2777: /// [`SpinLock`]: super::SpinLock
2778: pub struct RwLock<T  /* : ?Sized*/ , Guard /* = PreemptDisabled*/ > {
2779:     guard: PhantomData<Guard>,
2780:     /// The internal representation of the lock state is as follows:
2781:     /// - **Bit 63:** Writer lock.
2782:     /// - **Bit 62:** Upgradeable reader lock.
2783:     /// - **Bit 61:** Indicates if an upgradeable reader is being upgraded.
2784:     /// - **Bits 60-0:** Reader lock count.
2785:     lock: AtomicUsize<_, RwPerms<T>,_>,
2786:     // val: UnsafeCell<T>,
2787:     val: PCell<T>,
2788:     ghost_id: Ghost<RwId>,
2789: }
2790: 
2791: /// This invariant holds at any time, i.e. not violated during any method execution.
2792: closed spec fn wf(self) -> bool {
2793:     invariant on lock with (val, guard, ghost_id) is (v: usize, g: RwPerms<T>) {
2794:         // BITS VALUE
2795:         let has_writer_bit: bool = (v & WRITER) != 0;
2796:         let has_upgrade_bit: bool = (v & UPGRADEABLE_READER) != 0;
2797:         let has_max_reader_bit: bool = (v & MAX_READER) != 0;
2798:         // The total number of `try_read` attempts recorded in the lock atomic, including created `RwLockReadGuard`s
2799:         // and those who are trying, no matter they will succeed or fail.
2800:         let total_reader_bits: int = (v & MAX_READER_MASK) as int;
2801:         // The clamped value represented in the counter bits. This counts the maximum number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2802:         // NOTE: This does not mean there are actually this number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s. The actual number of successfully
2803:         // created/creating `RwLockReadGuard`s can be smaller than this number, because previously created `RwLockReadGuard`s may be dropped.
2804:         let reader_bits: int = if has_max_reader_bit { MAX_READER as int } else { (v & READER_MASK) as int };
2805: 
2806:         // ACTUAL NUMBER OF ACTIVE GUARDS.
2807:         // The number is tracked by the ghost resources remained in the lock.
2808:         // By active, we mean from the perspective the lock, the permissions for these guards are given out.
2809:         // The actual guards may be still being created, but they must be successfully created finally.
2810:         // This invariant maintains the consistency between the ghost resources and the lock atomic value.
2811: 
2812:         // Whether there is an active writer
2813:         let active_writer: bool = g.core_token.is_right();
2814:         // The number of active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, which can only be 0 or 1.
2815:         let active_upgrade_guard: bool = !active_writer && g.upreader_guard_token is None;
2816:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2817:         let active_read_guards: int = if g.read_guard_token is Left {
2818:             MAX_READER_U64 - g.read_guard_token.left().frac()
2819:         } else {
2820:             0
2821:         };
2822:         // The first `try_upread` that fails, which has not returned yet.
2823:         let pending_failed_upread_attempt: bool = g.upread_retract_token is None;
2824:         // The number of `try_read` attempts that will fail.
2825:         let failed_reader_attempts: int = V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS - g.read_retract_token.frac();
2826: 
2827:         &&& if g.core_token.is_left() {
2828:             g.read_guard_token is Left
2829:         } else {
2830:             &&& g.upreader_guard_token is None
2831:             &&& g.read_guard_token is Right
2832:         }
2833:         // The `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit is set iff there is an active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` or a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2834:         &&& has_upgrade_bit <==> (active_upgrade_guard || pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2835:         // An active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` cannot coexist with a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2836:         &&& !(active_upgrade_guard && pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2837:         // The `READER` bits count the number of all active read guards and pending failed `try_read` attempts.
2838:         &&& total_reader_bits == active_read_guards + failed_reader_attempts
2839:         // There is an active `RwLockWriteGuard` iff the `WRITER` bit is set.

2588: /// Half of the permission for read access, one for `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` and the other for all `RwLockReadGuard`s.

2591: /// The permission for read access can be further split into `MAX_READER` pieces.

2594: tracked struct RwPerms<T> {
2595:     /// This token tracks whether the write permission is given out. If it is `Left`, it stores the knowledge that
2596:     /// there are active readers because the existence of `HalfPerm` resource for read access.
2597:     /// If it is `Right`, we know there is an active writer and there is no active reader, because there is a `NoPerm`
2598:     /// indicating the absence of `PointsTo<T>`.
2599:     core_token: SumResource<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>,
2600:     /// The permission to retract a `READER` count. Its total quantity tracks the gap between
2601:     /// the number of `try_read` increments recorded in the lock atomic and the number of active
2602:     /// `RwLockReadGuard`s (created and ongoing creation that will succeed) represented by `read_guard_token`.
2603:     /// It can be splited up to `V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS:= 2 * MAX_READER` pieces,
2604:     /// which allows at most `2*MAX_READER - 1` `try_read` attempts that will fail to acquire the lock.
2605:     read_retract_token: TokenResource<V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS>,
2606:     /// The permission to retract the set of `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit.
2607:     upread_retract_token: Option<UniqueToken>,

2611:     /// If it is `Right`, it stores an empty token indicating the permission has been given out.
2612:     read_guard_token: Sum<
2613:         CountResource<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,

2701: struct_with_invariants! {
2702: /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2703: ///
2704: /// # Overview
2705: ///
2706: /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2707: /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2708: /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2709: /// read-only access.
2710: ///
2711: /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2712: /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2713: /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2714: /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2715: /// the cost of spinning.
2716: ///
2717: /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2718: /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2719: /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2720: /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2721: ///
2722: /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2723: /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2724: /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2725: /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2726: /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2727: /// while the lock is held.
2728: ///
2729: /// # Usage
2730: /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2731: /// but written to occasionally.
2732: ///
2733: /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2734: /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2735: ///
2736: /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2737: /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2738: ///
2739: /// # About Guard
2740: ///
2741: /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2742: ///
2743: /// # Examples
2744: ///
2745: /// ```
2746: /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2747: ///
2748: /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2749: ///
2750: /// // many read locks can be held at once
2751: /// {
2752: ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2753: ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2754: ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2755: ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2756: ///
2757: ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2758: ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2759: ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2760: ///     drop(r1);
2761: ///     drop(r2);
2762: ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2763: ///
2764: ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2765: ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2766: ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2767: ///     *w1 += 1;
2768: ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
2769: /// }   // upread lock are dropped at this point
2770: ///
2771: /// {
2772: ///     // Only one write lock can be held at a time
2773: ///     let mut w2 = lock.write();
2774: ///     *w2 += 1;
2775: ///     assert_eq!(*w2, 7);
2776: /// }   // write lock is dropped at this point
2777: /// ```
2778: ///
2779: /// [`SpinLock`]: super::SpinLock
2780: pub struct RwLock<T  /* : ?Sized*/ , Guard /* = PreemptDisabled*/ > {
2781:     guard: PhantomData<Guard>,
2782:     /// The internal representation of the lock state is as follows:
2783:     /// - **Bit 63:** Writer lock.
2784:     /// - **Bit 62:** Upgradeable reader lock.
2785:     /// - **Bit 61:** Indicates if an upgradeable reader is being upgraded.
2786:     /// - **Bits 60-0:** Reader lock count.
2787:     lock: AtomicUsize<_, RwPerms<T>,_>,
2788:     // val: UnsafeCell<T>,
2789:     val: PCell<T>,
2790:     ghost_id: Ghost<RwId>,
2791: }
2792: 
2793: /// This invariant holds at any time, i.e. not violated during any method execution.
2794: closed spec fn wf(self) -> bool {
2795:     invariant on lock with (val, guard, ghost_id) is (v: usize, g: RwPerms<T>) {
2796:         // BITS VALUE
2797:         let has_writer_bit: bool = (v & WRITER) != 0;
2798:         let has_upgrade_bit: bool = (v & UPGRADEABLE_READER) != 0;
2799:         let has_max_reader_bit: bool = (v & MAX_READER) != 0;
2800:         // The total number of `try_read` attempts recorded in the lock atomic, including created `RwLockReadGuard`s
2801:         // and those who are trying, no matter they will succeed or fail.
2802:         let total_reader_bits: int = (v & MAX_READER_MASK) as int;
2803:         // The clamped value represented in the counter bits. This counts the maximum number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2804:         // NOTE: This does not mean there are actually this number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s. The actual number of successfully
2805:         // created/creating `RwLockReadGuard`s can be smaller than this number, because previously created `RwLockReadGuard`s may be dropped.
2806:         let reader_bits: int = if has_max_reader_bit { MAX_READER as int } else { (v & READER_MASK) as int };
2807: 
2808:         // ACTUAL NUMBER OF ACTIVE GUARDS.
2809:         // The number is tracked by the ghost resources remained in the lock.
2810:         // By active, we mean from the perspective the lock, the permissions for these guards are given out.
2811:         // The actual guards may be still being created, but they must be successfully created finally.
2812:         // This invariant maintains the consistency between the ghost resources and the lock atomic value.
2813: 
2814:         // Whether there is an active writer
2815:         let active_writer: bool = g.core_token.is_right();
2816:         // The number of active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`, which can only be 0 or 1.
2817:         let active_upgrade_guard: bool = !active_writer && g.upreader_guard_token is None;
2818:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s.
2819:         let active_read_guards: int = if g.read_guard_token is Left {
2820:             MAX_READER_U64 - g.read_guard_token.left().frac()
2821:         } else {
2822:             0
2823:         };
2824:         // The first `try_upread` that fails, which has not returned yet.
2825:         let pending_failed_upread_attempt: bool = g.upread_retract_token is None;
2826:         // The number of `try_read` attempts that will fail.
2827:         let failed_reader_attempts: int = V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS - g.read_retract_token.frac();
2828: 
2829:         &&& if g.core_token.is_left() {
2830:             g.read_guard_token is Left
2831:         } else {
2832:             &&& g.upreader_guard_token is None
2833:             &&& g.read_guard_token is Right
2834:         }
2835:         // The `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit is set iff there is an active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` or a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2836:         &&& has_upgrade_bit <==> (active_upgrade_guard || pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2837:         // An active `RwLockUpgradeableGuard` cannot coexist with a pending failed `try_upread` attempt.
2838:         &&& !(active_upgrade_guard && pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2839:         // The `READER` bits count the number of all active read guards and pending failed `try_read` attempts.
2840:         &&& total_reader_bits == active_read_guards + failed_reader_attempts
2841:         // There is an active `RwLockWriteGuard` iff the `WRITER` bit is set.
2842:         &&& active_writer <==> has_writer_bit
2843:         // The number of active `RwLockReadGaurd`s is less than or equal to the `READER` bits.
2844:         &&& 0 <= active_read_guards <= reader_bits <= total_reader_bits
2845:         // The core invariant of `RwLock`: there are no simultaneous active writers and readers.
2846:         &&& !(active_writer && (active_read_guards + if active_upgrade_guard { 1int } else { 0 }) > 0)
2847:         &&& g.core_token.id() == ghost_id@.core_token_id
2848:         &&& g.core_token.wf()
2849:         &&& g.core_token.is_left() ==> {
2850:             &&& !g.core_token.is_resource_owner()
2851:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 1
2852:         }
2853:         &&& g.core_token.is_right() ==> {
2854:             let empty = g.core_token.resource_right();
2855:             &&& empty.id() == ghost_id@.frac_id
2856:             &&& g.core_token.frac() == 2
2857:             &&& g.core_token.has_resource()
2858:         }
2859:         &&& g.read_retract_token.wf()
2860:         &&& g.read_retract_token.id() == ghost_id@.read_retract_token_id
2861:         &&& g.upread_retract_token is Some ==>
2862:             {
2863:                 let token = g.upread_retract_token->0;
2864:                 &&& token.wf()
2865:                 &&& token.id() == ghost_id@.upread_retract_token_id
2866:             }
2867:         &&& g.upreader_guard_token is Some ==> {
2868:             let token = g.upreader_guard_token->0;
2869:             wf_upgradeable_guard_token(ghost_id@.core_token_id, ghost_id@.frac_id, val.id(), token)
2870:         }
2871:         &&& match g.read_guard_token {
2872:             Sum::Left(token) => {
2873:                 &&& token.wf()
2874:                 &&& token.id() == ghost_id@.read_guard_token_id
2875:                 &&& token.not_empty() ==> {
2876:                     let resource = token.resource();
2877:                     let read_half_cell_perm = resource.0;
2878:                     let mode_knowledge = resource.1;
2879:                     &&& mode_knowledge.id() == ghost_id@.core_token_id
2880:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.id() == ghost_id@.frac_id
2881:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.resource().id() == val.id()
2882:                     &&& read_half_cell_perm.frac() == 1
2883:                 }
2884:             },
2885:             Sum::Right(empty) => {
2886:                 &&& empty.id() == ghost_id@.read_guard_token_id
2887:             },
2888:         }
2889: 
2890:     }
2891: }
2892: 
2893: }

2987:     /// Acquires a read lock and spin-wait until it can be acquired.
2988:     ///
2989:     /// The calling thread will spin-wait until there are no writers or
2990:     /// upgrading upreaders present. There is no guarantee for the order
2991:     /// in which other readers or writers waiting simultaneously will
2992:     /// obtain the lock.
2993:     #[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]
2994:     pub fn read(&self) -> RwLockReadGuard<'_, T, G> {
2995:         loop {
2996:             if let Some(readguard) = self.try_read() {
2997:                 return readguard;
2998:             } else {
2999:                 core::hint::spin_loop();
3000:             }
3001:         }
3002:     }
3003: 
3004:     /// Acquires a write lock and spin-wait until it can be acquired.
3005:     ///
3006:     /// The calling thread will spin-wait until there are no other writers,
3007:     /// upreaders or readers present. There is no guarantee for the order
3008:     /// in which other readers or writers waiting simultaneously will
3009:     /// obtain the lock.
3010:     #[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]
3011:     pub fn write(&self) -> RwLockWriteGuard<'_, T, G> {
3012:         loop {
3013:             if let Some(writeguard) = self.try_write() {
3014:                 return writeguard;
3015:             } else {
3016:                 core::hint::spin_loop();
3017:             }
3018:         }
3019:     }

3021:     /// Acquires an upreader and spin-wait until it can be acquired.
3022:     ///
3023:     /// The calling thread will spin-wait until there are no other writers,
3024:     /// or upreaders. There is no guarantee for the order in which other
3025:     /// readers or writers waiting simultaneously will obtain the lock.
3026:     ///
3027:     /// Upreader will not block new readers until it tries to upgrade. Upreader
3028:     /// and reader do not differ before invoking the upgrade method. However,
3029:     /// only one upreader can exist at any time to avoid deadlock in the
3030:     /// upgrade method.
3031:     #[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]
3032:     pub fn upread(&self) -> RwLockUpgradeableGuard<'_, T, G> {
3033:         loop {
3034:             if let Some(guard) = self.try_upread() {
3035:                 return guard;
3036:             } else {
3037:                 core::hint::spin_loop();
3038:             }

2585: /// The token reserved in the lock when the write permission is given out.
2586: type NoPerm<T> = EmptyCount<PointsTo<T>>;

2588: type HalfPerm<T> = Count<PointsTo<T>>;
2589: /// The permission for read access can be further split into `MAX_READER` pieces.
2590: type ReadPerm<T> = (HalfPerm<T>, OneLeftKnowledge<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>);

2592: tracked struct RwPerms<T> {
2593:     /// This token tracks whether the write permission is given out. If it is `Left`, it stores the knowledge that
2594:     /// there are active readers because the existence of `HalfPerm` resource for read access.
2595:     /// If it is `Right`, we know there is an active writer and there is no active reader, because there is a `NoPerm`
2596:     /// indicating the absence of `PointsTo<T>`.
2597:     core_token: SumResource<HalfPerm<T>, NoPerm<T>, 3>,
2598:     /// The permission to retract a `READER` count. Its total quantity tracks the gap between
2599:     /// the number of `try_read` increments recorded in the lock atomic and the number of active
2600:     /// `RwLockReadGuard`s (created and ongoing creation that will succeed) represented by `read_guard_token`.
2601:     /// It can be splited up to `V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS:= 2 * MAX_READER` pieces,
2602:     /// which allows at most `2*MAX_READER - 1` `try_read` attempts that will fail to acquire the lock.
2603:     read_retract_token: TokenResource<V_MAX_READ_RETRACT_FRACS>,
2604:     /// The permission to retract the set of `UPGRADEABLE_READER` bit.

2610:     read_guard_token: Sum<
2611:         CountResource<ReadPerm<T>, MAX_READER_U64>,

2699: struct_with_invariants! {
2700: /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2701: ///
2702: /// # Overview
2703: ///
2704: /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2705: /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2706: /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2707: /// read-only access.
2708: ///
2709: /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2710: /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2711: /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2712: /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2713: /// the cost of spinning.
2714: ///
2715: /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2716: /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2717: /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2718: /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2719: ///
2720: /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2721: /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2722: /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2723: /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2724: /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2725: /// while the lock is held.
2726: ///
2727: /// # Usage
2728: /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2729: /// but written to occasionally.
2730: ///
2731: /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2732: /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2733: ///
2734: /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2735: /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2736: ///
2737: /// # About Guard
2738: ///
2739: /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2740: ///
2741: /// # Examples
2742: ///
2743: /// ```
2744: /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2745: ///
2746: /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2747: ///
2748: /// // many read locks can be held at once
2749: /// {
2750: ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2751: ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2752: ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2753: ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2754: ///
2755: ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2756: ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2757: ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2758: ///     drop(r1);
2759: ///     drop(r2);
2760: ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2761: ///
2762: ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2763: ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2764: ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2765: ///     *w1 += 1;
2766: ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
